To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed a formal model of chemosensatory signal transduction and that (2) this model is mathematically equivalent to an artificial neural network and that (3) this model is sufficient to simulate the response characteristics of receptor neurons from the general odor-processing subsystem in honeybees.

a model of olfactory signal transduction can be reformulated as an ANN, that ANNs are a useful tool to study olfactory signal transductions and to simulate data recorded in vivo, and that the model presented here is sufficient to simulate the complex response characteristics found in receptor neurons of the general odor-processing subsystem.

the model is able to simulate the nonlinear response characteristics of honeybees, and the nonlinear concentration dependencies and interaction effects of the model are sufficient to explain the nonlinear response characteristics.
